item.text: I’ll inspect the parser helper and its focused tests, then report whether the 64-character ASCII limit is enforced correctly. This is a local correctness review, so the Fructal workflow method does not activate.

The implementation checks ASCII encodability and then rejects lengths above 64; the focused boundary tests cover 64 and 65 characters. I’m running the suite with cache and bytecode writes disabled, then I’ll distinguish actual defects from minor coverage gaps.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python - <<'PY'
from parser import parse_ascii

assert parse_ascii('') == (True, '')
assert parse_ascii('a' * 64) == (True, 'a' * 64)
assert parse_ascii('a' * 65) == (False, 'maximum length is 64 characters')
assert parse_ascii('café') == (False, 'ASCII characters required')
for n in range(65):
    value = ''.join(chr(i % 128) for i in range(n))
    assert parse_ascii(value) == (True, value)
for n in (65, 66, 128):
    assert parse_ascii('x' * n)[0] is False
print('focused checks passed')
PY
nl -ba parser.py
